title: K-flat resolution with K-flat stalk
statement: Let C be a category essentially small in the coefficient universe, J a Grothendieck topology, R a sheaf of commutative rings, p a point of Sh(C,J), and s a normalized ringed-site point [def-sfb-ringed-site-point], with stalk ring A and module functor S. For any unbounded module complex K there exist P and a quasi-isomorphism q:P→K such that P is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and S(P) is K-flat over A [def-pc-module-kflat-complex].

proof.text: Use the constructed functorial flat resolution and its reduced left-resolution functor. The augmentation P→K is a quasi-isomorphism, P is categorically K-flat, and the independent-coefficient comparison makes it K-flat on the site. The reduced resolution has a countable filtered-colimit presentation by bounded-above complexes of flat terms.
The point module adjunction makes S preserve colimits. Each image complex remains bounded above, and its terms are flat by flat preservation. Hence each is K-flat over A.

The module category has exact filtered colimits and tensor preserves these colimits. K-flat objects are closed under the indicated filtered colimit; its value is S(P). This supplies the required resolution.

proof_origin.note: Formal proof supplied in full; generic singleton-site and universal-matrix arguments expand the cited source step.
